comment: Generated by runtime/http/go/serviceauth (cd runtime/http/go && go test ./serviceauth -run TestWriteParityVectors -update); do not edit. The Go, TypeScript and Rust HTTP runtimes each run every vector through their route gate (D37, docs/stack-model.md section 9.8). Per vector: build the service authenticator from configs[config] with the clock at now (unix seconds) and a fresh, empty key cache; config null means the server has no service authenticator. The key fetcher returns jwks[url] and fails for any other URL. Send headers (names are case-insensitive) to a route whose rule is route.service (null: no service clause; mode require or allow; from lists API names, empty lists every caller) and route.user. The service step verifies a Service-Authorization credential when present and answers a refusal at once, then applies the rule: require refuses no caller with 401 service_unauthorized and an unlisted one with 403 service_forbidden, then runs the user step; allow admits a listed caller without the user step; without a service authenticator a route with a rule answers 401 service_unauthorized. The end-user step is a stub, run when route.user.required: it looks up the Authorization Bearer token in users (absent or unknown: 401 unauthorized), then requires one of route.user.permissions to be covered by a granted permission under the dotted-path rule, a granted a covering a and a.b (else 403 forbidden). Compare status; code, the problem code of a refusal (null on 200); caller and user, what the handler saw (null unless 200; user is the stub's subject); userAuthenticated, whether the stub's lookup ran, refusing or not. No vector depends on the order of the end-user lookup and the service step on a route without a service clause, since the Go server authenticates the end user there first. Tokens are fixed: RS256 and EdDSA signatures are deterministic, and ES256 ones are RFC 6979 deterministic signatures.
